regenerate: see corpus/herdr-0.8.0/closing-reasons/, recorded by hand against a scratch daemon with three `herdr terminal session control` clients: one holding the terminal, one refused a plain attach, one taking it with --takeover
why: A bridge that stopped is one event to the app and several things to the person, and herdr says which only in prose - a `reason` string with no code beside it. Muster reads that prose in exactly one place, and this is the oracle for it: a herdr re-pin that rewords a closing reason silently turns a takeover into a lost connection, and two windows would then trade one terminal until both gave up. The endings are Muster's own words; the reasons are herdr's, quoted from the recording.

cases.name: a terminal that already has a client is a refusal
cases.why: The ordinary case after a relaunch: a herdr client whose transport died goes on holding the terminal, so a fresh app's first attach is refused by a machine that is otherwise healthy. The answer is to attach again and take it, which is the opposite of the answer below.

given.reason: terminal attach failed: terminal term_65a7828a5ca4f1 already has an attached client; retry with --takeover

cases.name: a terminal handed to somebody else is a takeover
cases.why: The one ending that must not be answered by attaching again. Another window asked for this pane and got it; taking it back would be answered the same way by the window on the other side.

cases.name: a client letting go is not a refusal of anything
cases.why: herdr's word for a stream whose stdin reached EOF. Nothing Muster runs releases a terminal deliberately, so this arriving means the bridge's own channel closed under it - which is a connection that went, and is answered by starting another bridge.

cases.name: a stream that ended with no closing frame is a lost connection
cases.why: What a dropped network looks like from inside the bridge: herdr's stdout simply ends. There is no reason to read, because there was no closing frame, and this is the case the whole replacement policy was written for.

cases.name: a reason nothing recognises is treated as a lost connection
cases.why: Prose matching stops matching when the prose changes, and the safe way to be wrong is to start another bridge: a wrong `lost` costs one extra attach, where a wrong `taken_over` leaves a pane dark on a healthy daemon and says nothing.

given.reason: the pane went to the shops
